title: client: `subscribeData` filters `data.record.restored` out, so an SDK data subscriber never sees a recycle-bin restore
body:
domain:spec#4 · marchtian · session_017ihL2eAG5J8aqAyPZif4BJ

Filing gate: ① a consumer gap found by the post-hoc spec review #31467 (a consumer note on the `Reviewed:` line for PR #31220 / #30237). The spec hunk itself is OK.
Reader: triage routes it (`packages/client`, the SDK).
Dedupe (open AND closed): "subscribeData restored" → no hit.
reach: an SDK client (`@objectstack/client`) that subscribes to an object's data events. A row restored from the recycle bin emits `data.record.restored` (`packages/objectql/src/recycle-bin/restore.ts:318`, via `publishDataEvent('restored')`), and the spec's `DataEventType` lists it. But `subscribeData` asks the server only for `created` / `updated` / `deleted`, so the restored row never reaches the subscriber's list.
type: Bug

## Readings (`origin/main` 3c380253e)

- `packages/client/src/realtime-api.ts` ≈L145-149: `eventTypes: ['data.record.created', 'data.record.updated', 'data.record.deleted']`.
- `packages/spec/src/api/events.zod.ts` (#31220) adds `data.record.restored` to the data event types. `realtime.test.ts:31-38` pins RealtimeEventType = DataEventType ∪ Bulk.

## Ask

Derive `subscribeData`'s `eventTypes` from the spec's `DataEventType` rather than a hand list, so the next added type cannot be dropped the same way. Add a client test asserting that a `data.record.restored` event reaches the callback.
